difference.question: How is AIPDD Canvas different from an ordinary AI video generator?
difference.answer: Ordinary tools work around a single prompt, a single clip, or a single image. AIPDD Canvas is built around a complete project: text import, asset build-up, episode planning, shot production and final compositing — a traceable, collaborative, reusable production loop.

gettingStarted.question: Where should I start the first time?
gettingStarted.answer: Follow the main workflow: import your text in Shrimp Feed, confirm characters / scenes / props / voices in Shrimp Pond, plan episodes and generate scripts and shots in Shrimp Lens, then export the cut from the compositing page. The first goal isn't perfection — it's getting one episode all the way through.

mirrorVsCanvas.question: What are Shrimp Lens and Shrimp Canvas each good for?
mirrorVsCanvas.answer: Shrimp Lens is the main production line: batch work, stability, episode-by-episode progress. Shrimp Canvas is the director's workbench: polishing key shots, exploring versions, finalising assets and heavier video work. On a real project, ordinary shots run through Shrimp Lens and the hard ones go to Shrimp Canvas.

canvasOverwrite.question: Do results in Shrimp Canvas overwrite my mainline assets automatically?
canvasOverwrite.answer: No. Anything generated or uploaded in Shrimp Canvas is a candidate by default. It only enters the project mainline once you explicitly commit it and pick a target slot — character, scene, prop, beat sketch, first frame or video.

whyAssetsFirst.question: Why organise characters, scenes, props and voices first?
whyAssetsFirst.answer: The usual cause of rework in AI video isn't the final generation step — it's unstable characters, vague scenes, props without references and inconsistent voices upstream. Turning those into assets in Shrimp Pond removes a lot of chaos from the shot stage.

contentTypes.question: What kinds of content is AIPDD Canvas suited to?
contentTypes.answer: AI short dramas, comic dramas, novel promos, commentary shows, ads, and training videos — plus team projects that maintain IP characters and serialised content over time. Solo creators can run the whole pipeline; teams can produce collaboratively.

teamRoles.question: How should a team divide the work?
teamRoles.answer: Split it by stage: the owner manages the project, cost and QA; the writer handles text and scripts; the art lead maintains characters, scenes and props; the storyboard/director owns shot performance; the video operator handles first frames, video and compositing. Permissions map to viewer, editor, admin and owner.

unstableResults.question: What should I check first when results are inconsistent?
unstableResults.answer: Find the stage that's failing: is the text clear, is the character identity right, do the scene and props have references, does the sketch describe the shot, is the first frame stable, does the audio match? Don't start by regenerating video over and over — fix the upstream assets and the shot description first.

dcUniverse.question: What does “Make Your DC Universe.” mean?
dcUniverse.answer: DC stands for each creator's own content universe. AIPDD Canvas is meant to help you start from one story and build up characters, world, scene assets and the ability to produce a series.

afterLogin.question: Where do I land after logging in?
afterLogin.answer: In the project hub. You can open an existing project or create a new one to start a new series. Each project is its own space, holding text, assets, episodes, shots, video, tasks and composited results.

macGatekeeper.question: macOS says the developer cannot be verified. Now what?
macGatekeeper.answer: Find AIPDD Canvas in Finder → Applications, Control-click the icon, choose Open, then confirm with Open in the dialog. You only do this once; after that it launches normally.

winSmartScreen.question: Windows says it protected my PC. Now what?
winSmartScreen.answer: Click More info, then Run anyway. SmartScreen blocks installers by default until they have enough downloads; it says nothing about whether this one is intact.

offline.question: Does the app still need an internet connection?
offline.answer: Yes. Script generation, first-frame rendering and video assembly all run on cloud compute; the app handles orchestration, media management and writing results to disk. Cuts already downloaded stay playable offline.

update.question: How do I upgrade?

storage.answer: Project data lives in the cloud with your account, so every device signed in sees the same episodes. Exported boards, first frames and finished cuts are written to local disk, and you can change that path in settings.

intro.body: This project bundles a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server named aipdd-drama. It wraps the AIPDD project API into a set of tools, so an AI client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex, etc.) can read project progress, scripts, characters and tasks in natural language, then drive the pipeline.
intro.note: Connecting requires the project dependencies (uv) installed on the host or inside a container, plus a valid API key. The URL and project id below are prefilled for the current project — copy as-is and adjust if needed.
intro.apiKeyHint: Generate the API key under Settings → API keys (st- prefix). The same key serves both MCP access and Model Plaza model calls — just replace <your-api-key> in the snippets.

step.configHint: Merge this snippet into your AI client's MCP config file (usually mcp.json / claude_desktop_config.json), then restart the client.
step.envHint: The MCP server uses these variables to decide which host to reach, which identity to use, and which project to operate on.
step.dockerHint: If the backend runs in Docker, let the client launch the server via docker exec into the api container — the snippet already carries the in-container API URL, a unified-key placeholder and the project id; swap in the key generated in Settings.

tools.imageGenerate: Generate an image from a prompt with optional reference images (freezone_gen).
tools.imageEdit: Edit an image with a prompt; result archived by default (freezone_edit).

tools.imageRelight: Relight an image from a reference or explicit light params.

tools.imageTemplateEdit: Run a fixed image template (nine-grid, three-view, storyboard grids, etc.).

tools.videoI2v: Generate a video from images (first frame or reference).

tools.audioMusic: Generate background music from a text description.
tools.textTranslate: Translate a text block by content kind.

tools.getRunStatus: Run status aggregate: pipeline progress plus running / failed / completed tasks and per-episode shot counts.
tools.cancelRun: Cancel running tasks: stop the in-flight tasks of an episode (a safety switch for fully-auto runs).
tools.suggestConfig: Smart defaults: recommend a generation config with rationale from the model catalog and aspect ratio, review before generating.

tools.post: Call a project POST API to submit processing.
tools.patch: Call a project PATCH API to update fields.
tools.delete: Call a project DELETE API to remove objects.

tools.pipelineStatus: Get the current project pipeline status and next step.
tools.listTasks: List the project's generation tasks and their status.

tools.episodeStory: Read an episode's story (the input for story-to-script).
tools.saveEpisodeStory: Save or update an episode's story and director style.

tools.storyToScript: Adapt an episode's story into a script and import it into the template (async task).
tools.ingestUploads: List files already uploaded to the script directory.
tools.buildCharacters: Extract characters from the knowledge graph (async task).
tools.updateCharacterFacePrompt: Update a character's face prompt before portrait generation.
tools.planIdentities: Plan character identities for an episode (async task).
tools.planScenes: Plan an episode's scene menu before sketch generation.
tools.planProps: Plan an episode's prop menu before sketch generation.
tools.generateScript: Generate the screenplay for one episode (async task).
tools.generateSceneMaster: Generate a scene's canonical master reference image.
tools.generateSceneReverse: Generate a scene's reverse master reference image.
tools.generateIdentityImage: Generate a character identity image (async task).
tools.generateSketches: Generate beat sketches for an episode (async task).
tools.detectSketchIdentities: Run episode-wide AI detection for identities and props.
tools.generateAudio: Generate an episode's audio with the current dubbing pipeline.
tools.startSingleVideo: Generate the video for a single beat (async task).
tools.renderFirstFrames: Render first frames for an episode (async task).
tools.composeEpisode: Compose / export the final video for an episode (async task).
tools.optimizeVideoGlobal: Run global video optimization for an episode (async task).
tools.getSketches: Read an episode's display-ready sketch URLs.
tools.getFirstFrames: Read an episode's display-ready first-frame URLs.
tools.getSketchCandidates: Read the sketch pool candidates for one beat.
tools.getSceneImages: Read a project's display-ready scene image URLs.
tools.getCharacterMedia: Read character portrait / identity image URLs.
tools.getEpisodeMedia: Read an episode's video / audio URLs.
tools.getFinalVideo: Read the composed final video for an episode.
tools.vectcutHealth: Check the VectCut editing service (draft folder, media roots, platform).
tools.vectcutCreateDraft: Create a blank Jianying/CapCut draft (canvas) and return its draft id.
tools.vectcutAddImage: Add an image (e.g. a storyboard frame) to the draft timeline.
tools.vectcutAddVideo: Add a video clip to the draft timeline.
tools.vectcutAddAudio: Add voice-over, BGM, or sound effects to the draft.
tools.vectcutAddText: Add a text overlay with optional styling and animations.
tools.vectcutAddSubtitle: Add SRT subtitles (file path, URL, or raw text).
tools.vectcutAddEffect: Add a scene/character video effect to the draft.
tools.vectcutAddSticker: Add a sticker to the draft by resource id.
tools.vectcutListOptions: List VectCut option names (transitions, masks, animations, effects, fonts).
tools.vectcutGetDuration: Get a media file duration in seconds.
tools.vectcutSaveDraft: Save the draft so it can be opened and polished in Jianying/CapCut.
tools.videoClone: Recreate a reference video end-to-end: keyframe analysis → per-shot remake → auto-concatenated film.
tools.videoMix: Mix a pool of images/videos into one narrated film with burned-in subtitles and BGM.
tools.whiteboardAnimation: Whiteboard animation: split a narration into AI-planned scenes, reveal each warm-beige sketch stroke by stroke and stitch it with the voice-over, rendered locally.
tools.explainerVideo: Science explainer: reference material → chaptered narration → per-shot motion graphics drawn frame by frame, then stitched with the voice-over, rendered locally.
tools.videoIdea: Turn a one-line idea into a short video: story / characters / storyboard → per-shot generation → stitched film.
tools.voiceClone: Batch-synthesize speech from text lines, with optional voice and audio model.
tools.musicCreate: Music creation: five MiniMax Music 3.0 modes (one-sentence / lyrics / instrumental / cover / humming), output archived into the library.
tools.lipSync: Make the person in a base video/image lip-sync to a driving audio track.
tools.replacePerson: Replace the person in a video with the character in a reference image.
tools.replaceProduct: Replace the product in a video with the product in a reference image.
tools.videoWatermark: Remove watermarks: local erase / Volcengine AI MediaKit / generative re-draw.

videoClone.title: Video Clone
videoClone.desc: Reference a video: auto-analyze the shots and recreate them shot by shot.
videoClone.modelHint: Frame reference or extra reference content requires model support for reference inputs (all_reference); text remaster can leave it empty to use the default model.
videoClone.planModelHint: Used for per-shot replication planning after frame analysis; frame analysis itself uses the system vision model and is not affected by this setting. Switch models to retry if the default channel is unavailable.
videoClone.referenceHint: Frame reference: keyframes from the source video serve as per-shot reference images; text remaster: regenerate purely from shot descriptions.
videoClone.referenceContentHint: Upload or pick reference images (character / scene / style) from the asset library; they act together with the prompt on the clone; enabling this requires model support for reference inputs (all_reference).
videoClone.referencePriorityHint: Subject replacement: only the reference content is submitted as reference image, so the on-screen subject follows it (source keyframes are dropped). Composition fidelity: source keyframes and reference content are submitted together, keeping the original framing and subject, although some models ignore the new subject in the reference content.
videoClone.audioGenerateHint: With model-generated audio, the reference video's speech is transcribed first and its lines are assigned verbatim into each shot prompt (measured: models only voice what the prompt says). Skipped automatically when the source has no audio track or no ASR channel is available.
videoClone.promptPlaceholder: Optional: extra style or content notes

videoMix.title: Short-Video Mix
videoMix.desc: Pick images/videos from the asset library as a material pool, add narration and subtitles, and mix them into one short video. The result is archived automatically.
videoMix.materialsHint: Segments are cut in pick order and loop to fill the video; images get a slow zoom, video clips are trimmed with source audio dropped. One submission produces one video.
videoMix.subject: Video topic
videoMix.subjectPlaceholder: e.g. Three reasons to camp in spring
videoMix.scriptPlaceholder: Leave empty to generate from the topic with AI
videoMix.needTopicOrScript: Enter a video topic or a narration script
videoMix.modelHint: Narration uses the selected speech model; mute mode needs neither narration nor subtitles.
videoMix.scriptModelHint: Used only when the narration script is auto-generated from the topic; follows the system configuration by default.
videoMix.subtitle: Burn subtitles
videoMix.maxDurationHint: Target length for mute mode, 5-600 s; leave empty to make one pass over the pool.

explainerClass.title: Explainer videos
explainerClass.desc: Two rendering styles for the same kind of narrated explainer: a whiteboard sketch revealed stroke by stroke, or chaptered motion graphics. Both need only the script or the reference material; visuals and voice-over are rendered locally.

whiteboardAnimation.title: Whiteboard animation
whiteboardAnimation.desc: Paste the narration, let the AI split it into scenes, draw each scene as a warm-beige sketch revealed stroke by stroke, then stitch it with the voice-over into one video. The result is archived automatically.
whiteboardAnimation.scriptPlaceholder: Paste the full narration to read aloud (1-10000 characters)
whiteboardAnimation.scriptHint: The copy is split into scenes; each scene gets one sketch revealed for its share of the voice-over.
whiteboardAnimation.textModelHint: Splits the copy into scenes and picks the key text per scene; follows the system configuration by default.
whiteboardAnimation.imageModelHint: Draws one warm-beige sketch per scene; empty uses the default image model.
whiteboardAnimation.voiceModelHint: The narrated duration drives each scene's reveal; empty uses the default voice engine.
whiteboardAnimation.subtitle: Burn subtitles

explainerVideo.title: Science explainer video
explainerVideo.desc: Paste reference material: the AI rewrites it into chaptered narration and plans the shots, then draws every frame as motion graphics and stitches it to the real voice-over length into one explainer film. The result is archived automatically.
explainerVideo.referencePlaceholder: Paste the topic brief, article or document body to explain (1-12000 characters)
explainerVideo.referenceHint: The narration is rewritten inside this material only and never invents facts; each shot's duration follows the actual read-aloud length.
explainerVideo.textModelHint: Rewrites the material into narration and plans each shot; defaults to the system text chain.
explainerVideo.voiceModelHint: The read-aloud length drives every shot's duration; empty uses the default voice engine.

videoIdea.title: Idea to Short Video
videoIdea.desc: Enter a one-line idea: the story is expanded, character portraits are extracted, scenes and camera shots are planned, then every shot is generated and stitched into a complete short video. The result is archived automatically.
videoIdea.ideaPlaceholder: e.g. A stray cat rescues a lost little girl on a rainy night
videoIdea.userRequirementPlaceholder: e.g. Suitable for children, warm ending
videoIdea.textModelHint: Used by the story, characters, script and storyboard steps; keep the system default unless its channel is unavailable, then pick another model to retry.
videoIdea.imageModelHint: Generates character portraits and the first/last frames of every shot; a model with strong character consistency works best.
videoIdea.videoModelHint: Turns each shot's first (and last) frame into video; a model supporting first-frame references works best.
videoIdea.totalDurationHint: AI plans the scene breakdown and storyboard from the total duration (scene count, shots per scene and shot duration are decided automatically).

voiceClone.title: Voice Clone
voiceClone.desc: Pick a voice, enter text line by line, synthesize speech in batch.
voiceClone.emptyLines: Enter at least one line of text
voiceClone.modelHint: Recommended: a speech model configured in the backend (e.g. IndexTTS2 / ElevenLabs); the audio model set in Settings → Default generation models is selected by default.

voiceReplace.sourceHint: The dialogue to be replaced is extracted from this; a video has its audio track demuxed locally first.
voiceReplace.referenceHint: Target timbre; the backend registers it as an account-level voice and clones timbre/prosody with IndexTTS2 zero-shot.
voiceReplace.asrHint: When left on auto, a ready candidate that accepts local audio is picked at execution time; FunASR needs a public audio URL, so it never applies to local replacement.
voiceReplace.asrHintSelected: This candidate transcribes the dialogue in the source, then the lines are re-synthesised with the reference timbre.
voiceReplace.asrNotConfigured: The selected ASR channel is not ready: finish its configuration under Settings → Models & Channels / VolcEngine Speech, or pick another candidate.

videoDubbing.title: Video dubbing
videoDubbing.desc: Upload the source video + a reference audio: extract the original lines (not translated), re-voice them in the original language with the reference timbre, then replace the whole audio track to output a dubbed video.
videoDubbing.modelHint: Pick a speech model configured in the backend (e.g. doubao-seed-audio / IndexTTS2); defaults to the audio model set under Settings → Default generation models.
videoDubbing.sourceHint: The lines to dub are extracted from this, and it also provides the picture for the output; its audio track is demuxed locally first.
videoDubbing.referenceHint: Target timbre; the backend registers it as an account-level voice and re-speaks the lines in the original language with a zero-shot timbre/prosody clone.
videoDubbing.languageHint: Only a pronunciation/language hint forwarded to the synthesis upstream (channels that support it honour it, others ignore it); the lines themselves are not translated.

musicCreate.title: Music Studio
musicCreate.desc: Five ways with MiniMax Music 3.0: one-sentence prompt, your own lyrics, instrumental, cover and humming-to-song. Outputs are archived to the library automatically.
musicCreate.modelHint: Candidates come from Settings → Models → Default generation models → Music. Cover and humming need a cover-capable model in the catalog (name contains cover); the other modes use a text-to-music model.

promptPlaceholder.one_sentence: e.g. A breezy summer folk track with a choral chorus and a whistling outro
promptPlaceholder.lyrics: e.g. Pop rock, clean drums, wide open chorus
promptPlaceholder.instrumental: e.g. Piano and strings instrumental, relaxed tempo, fits an intro
promptPlaceholder.cover: e.g. Turn this song into a rock version with heavier drums
promptPlaceholder.humming: e.g. Turn this humming into an upbeat folk cover

musicCreate.lyricsPlaceholder:
[Verse]
First verse line

[Chorus]
First chorus line
musicCreate.lyricsHint: {{n}} / {{max}} characters; [Verse] / [Chorus] structure tags are supported. Optional for covers — leave it empty and the upstream extracts lyrics from the original.
musicCreate.referenceHint: 6 seconds to 6 minutes, up to 50 MB, mp3 / wav / flac. Upload a file or pick one from the asset library.
musicCreate.preprocessHint: Want to rewrite the lyrics? Extract them first, edit, then submit. Submitting directly also works — the upstream extracts lyrics automatically.
musicCreate.featureHint: Cover feature ready (valid for 24 hours). Edit the lyrics and submit.
musicCreate.preprocessDone: Lyrics extracted — edit them and submit
musicCreate.providerHint: The international and China sites do not share API keys. Leave it empty to use the channel of the selected model; make sure the other site is configured in Settings before switching.
musicCreate.needLyrics: “From lyrics” requires lyrics. Use “One sentence” to generate from a description alone.
musicCreate.needReference: Cover and humming need a reference audio (the original track or your humming)

musicCreate.promptTooShort: The target style description needs at least {{min}} characters — say what it should become

musicCreate.extractedLyricsLength: Edited lyrics must be {{min}}–{{max}} characters (upstream limit for two-step covers)

lipSync.title: Lip-Sync Video
lipSync.desc: Choose a model and drive multiple bases (image/video) with one audio track in batch.
lipSync.modelHint: Recommended: a video model that supports omni reference (e.g. Seedance 2.0 / 2.5, MiniMax H3). The list is already filtered by this capability.

replacePerson.title: Replace Person
replacePerson.desc: Use omni-reference models (Seedance2+ / ap-minimax-h3, etc.) to replace the person in videos by reference image, in batch.
replacePerson.needImage: Upload a person reference image first
replacePerson.modelHint: Recommended: a video model that supports omni reference (e.g. Seedance 2.0 / 2.5, MiniMax H3). The list is already filtered by this capability.

replaceProduct.title: Replace Product
replaceProduct.desc: Use omni-reference models (Seedance2+ / ap-minimax-h3, etc.) to replace the product in videos by reference image, in batch.
replaceProduct.needImage: Upload a product reference image first
replaceProduct.modelHint: Recommended: a video model that supports omni reference (e.g. Seedance 2.0 / 2.5, MiniMax H3). The list is already filtered by this capability.

videoWatermark.title: Video Watermark Removal
videoWatermark.desc: Remove watermark/subtitles from multiple videos, auto-detect or box a region.
videoWatermark.dragHint: Drag on the preview to draw a box · drag inside to move · bottom-right handle to resize
videoWatermark.needVideoPreview: Upload a video to drag-select the region on its preview
videoWatermark.applyAll: The same box will apply to all {{n}} videos
videoWatermark.engineHintLocal: Runs ffmpeg on this machine: no network, no extra cost; quality is limited on complex backgrounds.
videoWatermark.engineHintMediakit: Cloud erasing on Volcengine AI MediaKit: high-frame-rate OCR + AIGC inpainting rebuilds the background seamlessly; works with auto-detect or box region.
videoWatermark.engineHintMediakitUnconfigured: MediaKit API key is not configured; submissions fall back to local erasing. Configure it in Settings → Models & Channels.
videoWatermark.engineHintSeedance: AI video editing: generative watermark removal per your instruction, best for complex scenes; uses the selected video model's quota.
videoWatermark.defaultPrompt: Remove the watermark and logo from the video, keeping the rest of the frame unchanged

imageWatermark.title: Image Watermark Removal
imageWatermark.desc: Remove watermarks from multiple images; you can add an instruction.
imageWatermark.defaultPrompt: Remove watermarks and logos, keep the rest of the image unchanged
imageWatermark.modelHint: Recommended: an image model that supports image-to-image (e.g. GPT Image 2, Seedream 4.5); keep the first catalog entry if unsure.

douyinCopywrite.title: Douyin Copy Extract
douyinCopywrite.desc: Paste a Douyin share link to parse the video and extract its spoken script; pick your own ASR model (gateway models, built-in FunASR or the Doubao Speech direct channel). The script is saved as a txt file.
douyinCopywrite.videoPlaceholder: Paste a link or the full share text from the Douyin app (any text containing the link works)
douyinCopywrite.videoHint: Full share text, short links or video URLs are all supported; the backend resolves the video ID automatically.
douyinCopywrite.needVideo: Paste a Douyin share link first
douyinCopywrite.needModel: Select an ASR model first: no default model is set, choose explicitly.
douyinCopywrite.modelHintChoose: No default ASR model: the list comes from the gateway's per-channel models (filtered for ASR) plus the built-in channels (FunASR / Doubao Speech direct); choose one explicitly.
douyinCopywrite.modelHint: Candidates come from the gateway model list across providers (ASR-family models) plus the built-in Doubao Speech direct channel; local audio is uploaded directly, so any video works.
douyinCopywrite.modelHintFunasr: The FunASR channel only accepts public audio URLs: it works only when the video exposes its original audio. Otherwise pick a gateway ASR model or the Doubao Speech direct channel.
douyinCopywrite.submittedHint: When done, the script shows in the result area below and is saved as a txt file.
douyinCopywrite.resultEmpty: The extracted script will appear here after you submit.

mediaCopywrite.title: Media Script Extract
mediaCopywrite.desc: Download from a link / upload a video / upload audio, separate the audio and transcribe the spoken script with the chosen ASR model (Douyin falls back through two channels); the script is saved as a txt file, and the downloaded video and separated audio are archived into the asset library automatically.
mediaCopywrite.linkPlaceholder: Paste a video share link or the full share text (any text containing the link works)
mediaCopywrite.linkHint: Supports YouTube / Bilibili / Kuaishou / Xiaohongshu / TikTok / Douyin and more; the backend downloads via yt-dlp, with a local-Chrome (CDP) dual-channel fallback for Douyin — no extra browser install needed.
mediaCopywrite.platformHint: The platform hints yt-dlp's extractor and toggles the Douyin dual-channel path; choose Other to let yt-dlp auto-detect.
mediaCopywrite.uploadVideoHint: Upload a local video file; the backend separates the audio then transcribes. Video and audio are archived into the asset library automatically.
mediaCopywrite.uploadAudioHint: Upload a local audio file and call ASR directly, skipping audio separation.
mediaCopywrite.modelHint: Candidates come from the gateway model list across providers (ASR-family models) plus the built-in Doubao Speech direct channel; local audio is uploaded directly, so any media works.
mediaCopywrite.modelHintPublicUrl: The {{channel}} channel only accepts public audio URLs: it works only when the media exposes publicly reachable original audio. Otherwise pick an ASR model that accepts a local upload.
mediaCopywrite.modelHintChoose: No default ASR model: the list comes from the gateway's per-channel models (filtered for ASR) plus the built-in channels (FunASR / Doubao Speech direct); choose one explicitly.
mediaCopywrite.submittedHint: When done, the script shows in the result area below and is saved as a txt file.
mediaCopywrite.resultEmpty: The extracted script will appear here after you submit.
mediaCopywrite.needModel: Select an ASR model first: no default model is set, choose explicitly.
mediaCopywrite.notConfiguredDoubao: Doubao Speech (VolcEngine ASR) credential is not configured: its API Key is NOT interchangeable with the gateway API key. Fill the API Key in the speech-recognition section of Settings → Model config → VolcEngine card before submitting.
mediaCopywrite.notConfiguredFunasr: The FunASR channel is not ready: complete the AIPDD channel Base URL / API key in Settings → Model config, or pick a gateway ASR model instead.

videoReverseScript.title: Video to Script
videoReverseScript.desc: Upload a video; the backend extracts key frames and the vision model you choose reverses them into a shot-by-shot script. The artifact is a plain-text txt script that never overwrites the existing story script.
videoReverseScript.uploadHint: Common video formats are supported; the backend extracts key frames with ffmpeg and feeds them to the vision model.
videoReverseScript.promptPlaceholder: Optional: e.g. "emphasize dialogue", "cut like a short drama" — sent to the model with the task brief.
videoReverseScript.modelHint: The list covers vision-capable models across gateway channels; keep the default to use the system vision model.
videoReverseScript.submittedHint: When it finishes, the script shows in the result area below and is saved as a txt file.
videoReverseScript.resultEmpty: After submitting, the reversed script appears here.

novelFormat.title: Premium drama format
novelFormat.intro: Premium drama scripts need explicit episode and scene boundaries. AIPDD Canvas splits the script by scene headers before generating visuals, dialogue, and audio line by line; it does not invent scene breaks for headerless prose.
novelFormat.standardStatusHint: Several industry formats are supported. Complete location, time, and INT/EXT metadata can be parsed reliably.
novelFormat.warningStatusHint: Scene boundaries are clear, but location, time, or INT/EXT metadata is incomplete and will be normalized.
novelFormat.blockingStatusHint: Import is blocked only when chapters are invalid or a premium drama has no recognizable scene headings.
novelFormat.repairableHint: Both scenes below are understood, but each is missing something: “SCENE 1 - TITLE” has no time or INT/EXT, and “INT./EXT.” cannot be resolved to a single interior/exterior value. Either one downgrades the whole script to “repairable” — import is allowed with a warning and the gaps are filled in later. The source text is never rewritten.
novelFormat.ruleEpisode: Start every episode with “EPISODE 1” on its own line; list multiple episodes in order. “CHAPTER 1” is accepted as well.
novelFormat.ruleScene: Give every scene a complete heading of its own: INT./EXT. + location + “ - ” + time, e.g. “INT. SEOUL SUBWAY STATION - NIGHT”. Do not fill the heading in only for the first scene of an episode.
novelFormat.ruleCharacters: List the characters physically present in the scene on a “Characters:” line right under the heading, separated by commas; keep identity and performance notes out of that line.
novelFormat.ruleBody: Write action on “△ ” lines, one visible shot per line (“▲” works too). Do not pack several shots or speakers onto one line.
novelFormat.ruleDialogue: Write dialogue as “JI-WON: Is anyone here?” — a bare uppercase character name on its own line is not recognized as a speaker. Add a short cue in parentheses only when needed, and use “JI-WON OS: …” for inner voice.
novelFormat.ruleLocationChange: Open a new scene heading whenever the physical location changes. Use INT. for interior and EXT. for exterior — a complete heading needs one of the two.
novelFormat.ruleTimeTokens: Only DAY, NIGHT, MORNING, AFTERNOON, EVENING, DAWN and DUSK are accepted in the time slot. Anything else (MIDNIGHT, LATE NIGHT, a bare clock time) makes the whole heading unrecognizable, so the scene boundary is lost.
novelFormat.ruleClockTime: Never put a clock time inside the location name. When you need one, add a separate “Time: 11:47 PM” line under the heading — the location stays “Seoul Subway Station” and the time normalizes to night.

missingSceneHeaders.message: No scene headings were recognized, so the system cannot tell where each scene begins.
missingSceneHeaders.fix: Follow the standard format: start every episode with “EPISODE N”, give each scene its own “INT./EXT. location - TIME” heading, then list characters, action, and dialogue. For example: EPISODE 1 / INT. City Cafe - DAY.

nonstandardSceneHeaders.message: Scene boundaries were recognized, but some scene metadata is incomplete.

sceneHeadersMissingTime.message: Some scene headings have no explicit time anchor, so time_of_day and scene variant inheritance may be unstable.
sceneHeadersMissingTime.fix: Add an explicit time to the scene heading. Only DAY, NIGHT, MORNING, AFTERNOON, EVENING, DAWN and DUSK are recognized. Scene boundaries are kept either way and normalized later.

missingInteriorExterior.message: The scene heading has no INT/EXT marker.
missingInteriorExterior.fix: Add INT or EXT, as in “location time INT/EXT”.

sparseSceneHeaders.message: There are few scene headings, so continuous scenes and time inheritance may be unstable.
sparseSceneHeaders.fix: Add one scene heading per scene.

tooFewDialogueLines.message: Few usable dialogue lines were found. If this is a silent or action-driven passage, you can still import it.
tooFewDialogueLines.fix: Add recognizable dialogue lines in the form “Character: line”.

multiSpeakerLines.message: Several lines pack multiple speakers or colons onto one line. The system will try to normalize them as a B-grade script, but one line per spoken line is better.
multiSpeakerLines.fix: Rewrite so each line holds a single spoken line from a single speaker.

ambiguousSpeakers.message: Many speakers are ambiguous (“he”, “she”, “the other party”, “the voice on the phone”), so identity resolution may be unstable.
ambiguousSpeakers.fix: Replace vague speakers such as “he” or “she” with the actual character names.

manyLongDialogues.message: There are many very long single dialogue lines, which tend to produce over-long single-unit dialogue later.
manyLongDialogues.fix: Split the longest lines to reduce the length of a single dialogue line.

duplicateChapterNumber.fix: Check for sentences in the body that look like chapter titles, so one chapter number is not split into several chapters.

nonIncreasingChapterNumber.message: The chapter number goes from {{previous_number}} back to or repeats {{number}}.
nonIncreasingChapterNumber.fix: Check that chapter numbers increase, or confirm that chapter-like wording in the body was not mistaken for a title.

notScreenplayLike.message: The text reads more like novel prose than a scene-based script. This check does not block the import, but the structured result may be weaker.
notScreenplayLike.fix: If this is novel prose, switch the project type to Narrated. If it is a script, add the scene headings.
